The Summit provided an important platform for advancing Ethiopia–Russia relations, strengthening Africa–Russia cooperation, and exploring new avenues of partnership in strategic sectors. (See article) Minister of Foreign Affairs Gedion Timothewos held discussions with China’s Special Envoy for African Affairs, Liu Xianfa, on Wednesday (November 4), exchanging views on peace and security in Africa. Minister Gedion briefed the Special Envoy on the current peace and security situation in the Horn of Africa, while Liu reaffirmed China’s commitment to playing a constructive role in promoting peace and security across the continent. FM Gedion held talks with Chinese Ambassador to Ethiopia Chen Hai on Tuesday (November 3), discussing ways to deepen the two countries’ All-Weather Strategic Partnership, particularly in trade, investment and capacity building. Ambassador Chen Hai reaffirmed China’s support for Ethiopia’s development plans. State Minister Ambassador Hadera Abera met with a delegation of the European Union Political and Security Committee (PSC), led by its Chair, Ambassador Lene Vensild, on Thursday (November 5). The discussion focused on current developments in Ethiopia, the Government’s reform efforts, regional peace and security, and Ethiopia-EU relations. State Minister Ambassador Berhanu Tsegaye received His Majesty King Letsie III of the Kingdom of Lesotho to Addis Ababa on Monday (November 2) at Bole International Airport, for his working visit to Ethiopia. Ethiopia participated in the 9th Assembly of the International Solar Alliance in New Delhi, represented by Ambassador Nebiyu Tedla, who reaffirmed the country’s commitment to renewable energy and highlighted the importance of cooperation, investment and affordable clean technologies in advancing an inclusive energy transition. Addis Ababa was recognized with the 2026 Global Award for Sustainable Development in Cities on Saturday (October 31), highlighting the city’s progress in sustainable urban development and its ongoing transformation. Djibouti President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh of Djibouti received Somalia’s Speaker of the House of the People, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur, on Monday (November 2), discussing ways to strengthen bilateral ties and strategic cooperation between the two countries. Africa and the African Union Africa’s Commemoration of the 40th Anniversary of the United Nations Declaration on the Right to Development at the African Union Headquarters, running from November 4-6. Convening under the urgent theme “From Resilience to Sustainable Prosperity,” the high-level opening session featured addresses from Ambassador Hadera Abera, State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Awa Dabo, United Nations Deputy High Commissioner for Human Rights, and Ambassador Bankole Adeoye, AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security. (See article) Senior officials from the African Union, the European Commission and EU Member States convened at the AU Headquarters in Addis Ababa on Wednesday (November 4) for the AU-EU Senior Officials’ Meeting, advancing the outcomes of the 7th AU-EU Summit held in Luanda in November 2025. The meeting focused on strengthening cooperation in peace and security, multilateralism, trade, economic development, climate action, food security, and digital and AI governance, with a view to translating the Joint Vision for 2030 into concrete actions. (See article) The African Union Commission and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies convened a high-level event on Tuesday (November 3) to advance durable solutions towards zero hunger in Africa, with AU Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf calling for collective action and sustained commitment to resilient agrifood systems and food security across the continent. AU Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf received King Letsie III of Lesotho on Tuesday (November 3), on the sidelines of the AU-IFRC High-Level Event on Advancing Durable Solutions Towards Zero Hunger in Africa. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Leads Ethiopian Delegation to the 3rd Russia–Africa Summit A high-level Ethiopian delegation led by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed successfully concluded its participation in the Third Russia–Africa Summit, held in Moscow, Russia, on October 28–29, 2026. The Summit provided an important platform for advancing Ethiopia–Russia relations, strengthening Africa–Russia cooperation, and exploring new avenues of partnership in strategic sectors. The Summit concluded with the adoption of the Declaration of the Third Russia–Africa Summit and a new Action Plan for the Russia–Africa Partnership Forum, setting out priorities for cooperation and continued political dialogue between the two sides. Addressing the plenary session of the Leaders’ Summit, Prime Minister Abiy highlighted the historic foundations of Ethiopia–Russia relations, noting that the friendship between the two countries spans more than a century and is rooted in mutual respect, cooperation, and solidarity. Recalling Russia’s humanitarian contribution following the Battle of Adwa in 1896, the Prime Minister noted that the Russian Red Cross Mission provided medical assistance to wounded Ethiopian soldiers and translated a medical guide into Amharic. He described this historical contribution as a meaningful example of knowledge exchange and solidarity between the two nations. The Prime Minister went on to emphasize that Ethiopia’s development priorities are anchored in three strategic pillars: food security, energy, and knowledge. He underscored the importance of strengthening agricultural productivity through cooperation in farm machinery, agro-processing, and industrial development. On energy cooperation, he highlighted Ethiopia’s engagement with Russia towards the development of the country’s first nuclear power plant, emphasizing the importance of diversifying the national energy mix, strengthening local technical expertise, and adhering to the safety standards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). He also pointed to the broader applications of nuclear science in healthcare, including cancer treatment. Regarding knowledge and technological development, the Prime Minister highlighted Ethiopia’s ambition to advance artificial intelligence capabilities through the establishment of Medemer University of Artificial Intelligence in Addis Ababa. He invited Russian universities and research institutions to collaborate with their Ethiopian counterparts in education, research, and technological innovation. He further called for stronger economic cooperation through joint ventures in Ethiopia’s special economic zones, particularly in pharmaceuticals and machinery, while underscoring the importance of facilitating trade and developing efficient payment channels. On regional and international affairs, Prime Minister Abiy reiterated Ethiopia’s support for African-led mediation and negotiated solutions to conflicts on the continent. He also welcomed the adoption of the new Action Plan, stressing the need to translate summit commitments into measurable results. The Prime Minister concluded by expressing Ethiopia’s readiness to host the next Russia–Africa Summit in Addis Ababa, the seat of the African Union, underscoring the country’s commitment to strengthening the partnership between Africa and Russia. As part of his engagements in Moscow, PM Abiy attended the airshow and handover ceremony marking the delivery of the first twelve Su-35 4++ generation fighter jets to the Ethiopian Defense Force. In his remarks on the occasion, the Prime Minister described the delivery as an important milestone in Ethiopia’s efforts to strengthen its defense capabilities and safeguard national sovereignty. He stated that the acquisition was made in accordance with an earlier agreement with the Russian Government and expressed appreciation to Russian President Vladimir Putin for facilitating the delivery ahead of the agreed schedule. The Prime Minister also indicated that Ethiopia would receive four batteries of the S-400 air defense system. He underscored that strengthening the operational readiness of the Ethiopian Defense Force is an essential component of the country’s efforts to deter aggression, safeguard its security, and contribute to regional stability. Expanding beyond strategic and military cooperation into the cultural and intellectual sphere, the visit also featured the presentation of the Russian-language edition of the Prime Minister’s foundational philosophy book, Medemer. During their bilateral discussions, Prime Minister Abiy handed over a copy of the newly translated book to President Vladimir Putin. On the sidelines of the Summit, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ambassador Hadera Abera held discussions with Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation Georgy Borisenko. Their discussions focused on strengthening the Ethiopia–Russia strategic partnership, expanding economic and energy cooperation, and enhancing collaboration on regional peace, security, and multilateral issues. Another significant outcome of the Summit was the signing of three bilateral agreements between Ethiopia and Russia. The agreements comprise an Intergovernmental Agreement on Dejazmach Balcha Hospital in Addis Ababa, a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ethiopian News Agency (ENA) and Russia’s ITAR-TASS, and another Memorandum of Understanding between ENA and Russia Today (RT). The agreement concerning Dejazmach Balcha Hospital underscores the shared commitment of the two countries to strengthening healthcare cooperation, modernizing medical infrastructure, and improving the delivery of health services. The two media cooperation agreements are expected to provide a framework for enhanced information exchange, professional collaboration, and institutional partnerships between the respective media organizations. Ethiopia Commemorates 40th Anniversary of the Right to Development with UN and AU Officials Africa’s Commemoration of the 40th Anniversary of the United Nations Declaration on the Right to Development at the African Union Headquarters, running from November 4-6. Convening under the urgent theme “From Resilience to Sustainable Prosperity,” the high-level opening session featured addresses from Ambassador Hadera Abera, State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Awa Dabo, United Nations Deputy High Commissioner for Human Rights, and Ambassador Bankole Adeoye, AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security. In his address, Ambassador Hadera Abera said the gathering was not merely a moment to mark a historical milestone, but an opportunity to reflect on four decades of achievements and to deliberate on what remains to be done to fully realize the Declaration’s objectives. He recalled the vision set out in its first article: that every human person should participate in, contribute to, and enjoy economic, social, cultural and political development, alongside the full realization of human rights and fundamental freedoms. The Ambassador acknowledged the progress the world has made since 1986, citing reduced extreme poverty, improved access to education and health care, longer life expectancy, and advances in science and technology. He noted, however, that the global South continues to face structural impediments, including external debt burdens and technological and financing gaps, which weigh on the development prospects of States operating in a rapidly evolving global landscape. Ambassador Hadera underscored that the Declaration affirmed a truth African visionaries had long understood: development is not a privilege, nor mere charity or aid, but a fundamental human right owed to every citizen. He pointed out that Africa had anchored this principle in the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights well before 1986, demonstrating that economic and social progress must advance together with civil liberties. Today, he said, the right continues to drive the African Union’s Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want, as well as the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Describing the theme as fitting for Ethiopia’s ongoing development trajectory, the Ambassador said Ethiopia, as a founding member of both the OAU and the UN, has consistently championed the view that true self-determination is inseparable from economic independence, food security, and self-reliant national development. Human dignity, he stressed, cannot be fully realized without freedom from poverty and access to quality healthcare, clean energy, education, and meaningful economic opportunity. He said Ethiopia’s home-grown economic reform agenda has taken historic steps toward economic resilience, environmental sustainability, and food sovereignty, translating the right to development from paper into tangible outcomes for its people. Through targeted investments in cluster farming, wheat self-sufficiency programs, and irrigation, he said, Ethiopia has moved from being a net importer to an exporter of wheat. The Ambassador also pointed to the Green Legacy Initiative, under which about 56 billion tree seedlings have been planted since 2019, restoring degraded lands, fighting climate change, and building sustainable livelihoods for rural communities. By integrating fruit-bearing and livestock fodder trees into local farming systems, he said, the initiative also advances food security. He described the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), Africa’s largest hydroelectric dam, planned and financed through Ethiopian capacity, as a project that is generating electricity to connect the region and embodies a model of self-reliance and shared, sustainable growth. GERD, he said, is an answer to Ethiopians’ centuries-old quest to use their resources for their own advancement, and a remarkable transformative project in Africa’s modern development history. It stands as a testament to Ethiopia’s commitment to the right to development and a practical embodiment of the Declaration’s core principle that citizens are the owners and primary beneficiaries of development’s fruits. “These initiatives prove that when a nation invests in its people, infrastructure, and natural resources, the Right to Development becomes a living reality,” he said. Speaking candidly about the realities facing the continent, Ambassador Hadera pointed to severe systemic obstacles: an unfair global financial system, crushing debt burdens, geopolitical shocks, and the disproportionate impacts of a climate crisis Africa did not create. These structural inequities, he said, strain the continent’s ability to make progress. Even so, he insisted that Africa is not a passive recipient of circumstances. Its greatest strengths lie within its own borders: a vibrant, innovative youth population, dynamic entrepreneurs, and unmatched natural wealth. He called on African countries to unlock the power of youth, empower women, and build resilient economies that leave no one behind, aligning efforts and moving forward together. At the same time, he urged continued demands for urgent reform of the global financial architecture. Africa, he said, requires equitable access to capital, fair trade systems, and robust climate adaptation financing so that its development strategies can flourish unhindered by external systemic imbalances. Concluding his remarks, Ambassador Hadera said development rights must not remain abstract concepts; they must be felt in family homes, children’s classrooms, and young people’s everyday businesses. He called the commemoration an occasion for renewed international solidarity, stronger domestic policies, and active partnerships among governments, civil society, and the private sector, urging participants to forge bold commitments that deliver tangible, lasting progress for every African citizen. Also addressing the session, Deputy High Commissioner Awa Dabo said the story of the right to development cannot be told without Africa. Long before development was firmly established in the global human rights discourse, she noted, African leaders, jurists, and civil society were advancing its essential foundations, including self-determination, sovereignty over natural resources, equitable participation, and international solidarity. “Africa was not simply a beneficiary of the right to development,” she said. “Africa was one of its principal architects.” She pointed to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights as the legally binding expression of this vision, and said Africa’s voice today is not only relevant but indispensable. Forty years on, she warned, formidable barriers remain, among them unequal trading relationships, unsustainable debt, shrinking development finance, and persistent illicit financial flows, with consequences felt most sharply by people already facing poverty, exclusion, and discrimination. Growth achieved at any cost to people and the planet, she stressed, is not development. Describing Agenda 2063 as a powerful roadmap, the Deputy High Commissioner said the task now is implementation: integrating the right to development into national plans, public budgets, monitoring systems, and accountability frameworks. She said the conference’s proposed Addis Ababa Outcome Statement offers a chance to set concrete commitments on domestication, financing, monitoring, and accountability. She added that implementation also depends on international cooperation, noting Africa’s leadership in advancing discussion of a draft international covenant on the right to development. The right, she cautioned, must not be reduced to an adversarial North-South debate, because it is a universal human right relevant to every society and every person. In his opening statement, Ambassador Bankole Adeoye recalled that the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights entered into force six weeks before the UN adopted the Declaration in 1986. Africa, he said, did not wait for the world to proclaim this right, because through Article 22, which recognizes the right of all peoples to economic, social and cultural development, it had already made it binding treaty law. He said the theme captures both Africa’s pride and its impatience, and stressed that resilience must never become the ceiling of its ambition. Ambassador Adeoye said the African Union supports a robust, legally binding International Covenant on the Right to Development. “Declarations inspire, but obligations deliver,” he said. He underscored that Agenda 2063 and its Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan translate Article 22 into measurable outcomes, which must be domesticated in national plans, budgets, and accountability systems. He also noted that in August 2026, the Peace and Security Council requested the integration of human rights indicators into the Continental Early Warning System. On the green transition, the Commissioner said Africa will not accept one that repeats the injustices of past extraction, and called for responsible business conduct, fair financing, debt sustainability, and action against illicit financial flows. He added that artificial intelligence must be governed by equality, participation, transparency, and accountability. Concluding, he said the right to development must be fulfilled “no

ethiopia.title: AU Commission Chief Urges Parties to Focus On Serving Citizens and Strengthening Nat'l Interests
ethiopia.content: Africa: AU Commission Chief Urges Parties to Focus On Serving Citizens and Strengthening Nat'l Interests - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Africa: AU Commission Chief Urges Parties to Focus On Serving Citizens and Strengthening Nat'l Interests 6 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Political parties must go beyond seeking power and focus on serving citizens, strengthening democratic governance and building consensus on Africa's development priorities, African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said today. Addressing the second African Political Parties Summit 2026 underway in Addis Ababa, the Chairperson highlighted the central role of political parties in advancing democratic governance, peace and development in line with the African Union Agenda 2063. Youssouf said political parties have three major responsibilities: developing social and economic policies that serve citizens, building bridges between citizens and state institutions, and raising awareness about the broader interests of their countries. "Are they meant to conquer power? Or is the mission wider than that?" he asked, stressing that political parties should serve the public and promote national interests rather than narrow political, ethnic or sectarian interests. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn The Chairperson also underscored the role of opposition parties in monitoring government actions and ensuring public accountability. On constitutional governance, Youssouf said states have a fundamental responsibility to protect their constitutions, organize credible elections and ensure respect for fundamental freedoms. "In case of disagreements on those critical issues, dialogue must always prevail," he noted. He further highlighted the importance of transparency in political party financing, saying strict rules are necessary to prevent corruption and external influences. Referring to the African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance, the Chairperson said the instrument recognizes political pluralism and promotes the rights and responsibilities of ruling and opposition parties. He also described the Maputo Protocol as an important foundation for women's participation in political life, emphasizing the need for forums bringing together women and young people to promote greater access to political participation and decision-making. Youssouf stressed that African citizens must be involved in decisions affecting their communities. Turning to Africa's economic future, he described political parties as architects of the continent's future, emphasizing the need for institutions capable of shaping that future around the general public interest rather than partisan considerations. Cooperation in these areas should be strengthened through open debate and citizens' oversight of public affairs, he added. ethiopia.content: Ethiopia, France Vow to Deepen Military and Strategic Cooperation - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia, France Vow to Deepen Military and Strategic Cooperation 6 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Ethiopia and France have pledged to deepen their longstanding military and strategic cooperation, with renewed emphasis on military capacity building, knowledge transfer and regional peace and stability. The commitment was made during talks between Ethiopian Defense Minister Mohammed Idris and French Ambassador to Ethiopia Alexis Lamek in Addis Ababa on Wondsday. The meeting, part of the Defense Minister's ongoing military diplomacy engagements with foreign ambassadors, focused on strengthening the two countries' historical ties and expanding cooperation in military and strategic affairs. Minister Mohammed expressed appreciation for France's support in enhancing Ethiopia's military capabilities through knowledge transfer, strengthening institutional capacity and improving its preparedness for peacekeeping operations. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn He also called on France to support Ethiopia's efforts to safeguard its legitimate and equitable interests in the region. On the ongoing Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (DDR) process in the Tigray Region, the Minister urged France to extend the necessary support to ensure its successful implementation. Ambassador Lamek, for his part, reaffirmed France's commitment to strengthening its longstanding relations and multifaceted cooperation with Ethiopia. He underscored his country's readiness to enhance joint efforts in promoting regional peace and stability, while advancing military training and capacity-building cooperation. The renewed commitment signals both countries' interest in translating their longstanding diplomatic relations into stronger practical cooperation in defense, military development and regional security, as ENA learned. ethiopia.title: PM Abiy Urges African Political Parties to Prioritize Leadership Renewal, Long-Term Dev't
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: PM Abiy Urges African Political Parties to Prioritize Leadership Renewal, Long-Term Dev't - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: PM Abiy Urges African Political Parties to Prioritize Leadership Renewal, Long-Term Dev't 6 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed called on African political parties to embrace leadership renewal and build consensus on long-term national priorities. He also stressed that the continent's development must transcend electoral cycles and changes of government. The Prime Minister made the call while opening the Second African Political Parties Summit in Addis Ababa, where he proposed two key commitments for inclusion in the Addis Ababa Declaration: establishing consensus on long-term national development priorities and strengthening leadership development and succession across Africa. He emphasized that political parties should agree on strategic national goals with measurable milestones to ensure continuity of development efforts regardless of political transitions. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn PM Abiy elaborated that parties can maintain ideological and policy differences and compete for electoral support while working together on fundamental national interests and long-term development objectives. He also stressed that leadership succession is essential to sustaining development, warning that countries risk losing hard-won progress when incumbent leaders fail to prepare the next generation of leadership. Highlighting Ethiopia's experience in political inclusiveness, the Prime Minister said the country's reformed government has incorporated leaders from opposition political parties. This reflects an approach that values broader participation and shared responsibility, the Premier revealed. He noted that Ethiopia's Medemer philosophy encourages political actors to recognize and build on one another's contributions despite their differences, particularly when national interests call for collective action. Turning to economic transformation, PM Abiy outlined key measures undertaken through Ethiopia's Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda, including opening the telecommunications, banking and competition sectors to foreign participation and introducing a market-based foreign exchange system. He also highlighted the Green Legacy Initiative, noting that more than 50 billion seedlings have been planted since its launch in 2019 through the collective participation of citizens, communities and institutions. The initiative, he explained, is aimed at restoring degraded landscapes, protecting water resources and strengthening national resilience to climate-related challenges, including droughts and floods. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia: Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) Engagement with Civil Society Organizations to Advance Agricultural Development - Africa.com
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) Engagement with Civil Society Organizations to Advance Agricultural Development | africa.com africa.com Support Us Subscribe to Our Newsletter African Nations Arts, Culture & Society Doing Business in Africa Engage & Learn Features & Opinion What's Happening Knowledge Partners Latest News More African Nations Arts, Culture & Society Doing Business in Africa Engage & Learn Features & Opinion What's Happening Knowledge Partners Latest News More Home / APO / Ethiopia Ministry Of Agriculture Moa Engagement With Civil Society Organizations To Advance Agricultural Development ← APO Group / Africa Newsroom Press release APO Group · 6 November 2026 Ethiopia: Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) Engagement with Civil Society Organizations to Advance Agricultural Development The Ministry of Agriculture has reaffirmed the critical role of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) in advancing agricultural development, emphasizing that their active engagement is essential for consolidating and sustaining the gains achieved in the sector. To strengthen collaboration and partnership, the Ministry convened a consultative meeting with international and local Civil Society Organizations operating in the agricultural sector. Opening the event, Mr. Yilma Sisay, Head of the Minister’s Office at the Ministry of Agriculture Ethiopia, underscored the importance of collaboration between the government and development partners in achieving Ethiopia’s national development and prosperity goals. He noted that international and local CSOs have a significant role to play in supporting the country’s agricultural transformation agenda. Mr. Yilma highlighted that the government has designed and is implementing strategic national programs aimed at ensuring food sovereignty and improving agricultural productivity. He stressed that the initiatives and work plans of development partners should be aligned with the country’s agricultural policies and sector development priorities. He also commended the valuable contributions of Civil Society Organizations toward improving the livelihoods of farmers and pastoralist communities, calling on them to further strengthen their coordination and collaboration with the Ministry. “The achievements recorded so far can only be sustained through stronger partnerships and coordinated efforts,” he remarked, reaffirming the Ministry’s commitment to providing the necessary support to organizations working in the sector. Speaking on the occasion, Mulugeta Deme (PhD), Director of the Programs and Projects Coordination Unit at the Ministry of Agriculture, stated that the workshop was organized to establish a structured platform that enables Civil Society Organizations to work more closely with the Ministry, while enhancing coordination, monitoring, and institutional support mechanisms. During the workshop, participants received presentations on key areas including agricultural and rural development policy, institutional reform initiatives, the mandate and responsibilities of the Programs and Projects Coordination Unit, major agricultural programs and projects being implemented by the Ministry, and the nationwide engagement and coverage of Civil Society Organizations in the agricultural sector. The meeting is expected to deepen cooperation between the Ministry and Civil Society Organizations, fostering a more coordinated and effective contribution to Ethiopia’s agricultural development objectives. ethiopia.title: UN Report Says UAE Firm Hired Colombian Mercenaries to Fight in Sudan, Raising Questions Over Abu Dhabi's UN Chief Bid
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: UN Report Says UAE Firm Hired Colombian Mercenaries to Fight in Sudan, Raising Questions Over Abu Dhabi's UN Chief Bid - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: UN Report Says UAE Firm Hired Colombian Mercenaries to Fight in Sudan, Raising Questions Over Abu Dhabi's UN Chief Bid 6 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba - A confidential UN report reportedly details how an Abu Dhabi-based security company with links to the Emirati ruling family recruited and deployed hundreds of Colombian former military personnel to fight alongside Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, intensifying questions over the UAE's nomination of diplomat Lana Nusseibeh to lead the United Nations. The report, submitted to the UN Security Council in early November and disclosed by The New York Times on November 5, identifies Global Security Services Group (GSSG), an Abu Dhabi-based private security company, as the principal recruiter and facilitator of the Colombian fighters, according to the newspaper's account. The findings add to mounting evidence of external military and logistical support sustaining the RSF in its war against the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), which erupted in April 2023. The war has devastated the country, killing tens of thousands of people, displacing millions and triggering widespread atrocities, particularly in Darfur. GSSG and the alleged recruitment network Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines According to the report, GSSG recruited hundreds of former Colombian military personnel and organized them into an operational battalion known as the "Desert Wolves" or "Lobos del Desierto." The fighters reportedly served in several military capacities, including infantry operations, artillery, drone operations, vehicle deployment and training of RSF combatants. The company is described as having close political, business and familial connections to senior figures in the UAE leadership. It was founded by a senior official in the UAE Presidential Court, while its business activities reportedly include providing security services to government ministries, including Foreign Affairs and Presidential Affairs. The recruitment operation involved moving Colombian fighters through a network of transit points connected to Emirati allies and partners. The routes included Bosaso in Somalia and areas of eastern Libya controlled by forces aligned with military commander Khalifa Haftar, before the fighters were transported into Sudan. The latest disclosures also build on earlier UN investigations indicating that Colombian contractors received military training at two facilities in the UAE before deployment. A July 2026 report by UN investigators reportedly documented the training arrangements but was not made public following objections at the Security Council. The New York Times reported that Bahrain objected to its publication, allegedly at the UAE's request. Abu Dhabi rejected suggestions that it had sought to influence Bahrain. The newly disclosed findings provide a more detailed account of the alleged recruitment and deployment network, extending scrutiny beyond the previously documented allegations of weapons, drones and other military assistance to the RSF. The scale of the operation is also significant. Earlier investigations cited estimates ranging from several hundred to approximately 2,000 Colombian contractors deployed over time. Fighters linked to the El Fasher offensive The reported deployment is particularly consequential because Colombian contractors were allegedly involved in RSF operations around El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur, during its prolonged siege and eventual capture in October 2025. The RSF's takeover followed more than 500 days of siege and was accompanied by widespread killings, sexual violence, abductions and other abuses against civilians. UN investigators have said the assault bore the "hallmarks of genocide." The presence and role of foreign fighters in the offensive have been documented through multiple investigations, including witness accounts, social media footage, geolocation analysis, corporate records and interviews with former contractors. A July 2026 UN experts' report said Colombian mercenaries established a base in Nyala in March 2025 and participated in operations supporting the RSF's campaign around El Fasher. The contractors reportedly operated drones and assisted with military planning during the siege and capture of the city. The allegations also raise concerns over the recruitment and training of children by RSF forces, with previous investigations pointing to foreign contractors' involvement in training activities involving child soldiers. Such recruitment and use of children in hostilities are prohibited under international law. Human Rights Watch findings The latest report follows earlier investigations by human rights organizations and international media documenting the alleged recruitment and deployment of Colombian fighters through UAE-linked networks. In a comprehensive 83-page report published on May 25, 2026 , titled From Bogotá to El Fasher: The UAE's Role in the Deployment of Colombian Fighters and Other Backing to the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan⁠ , Human Rights Watch (HRW) documented how GSSG apparently hired hundreds of Colombian former military personnel from 2024 onwards. HRW found that a Colombia-based recruitment agency, A4SI, recruited the contractors, who subsequently signed contracts with GSSG and were transferred through UAE military facilities, including Ghiyathi and Al Wathba, before being deployed to Sudan. The organization examined interviews with former contractors, residents of El Fasher, corporate records, employment documents, photographs, videos and geolocation data. It concluded that the evidence indicated the UAE was assisting or substantially contributing to the RSF's capacity to commit serious violations of international humanitarian law . HRW called for investigations into GSSG and individuals involved in the recruitment network, possible targeted sanctions, and measures to end external military support to the RSF. The latest UN disclosures further reinforce the concerns raised in those investigations, particularly regarding the connections between private security companies, state-linked actors and the cross-border military networks sustaining Sudan's conflict. UAE candidate's UN secretary-general bid faces renewed scrutiny The timing of the disclosures presents a fresh diplomatic challenge for the UAE as it seeks to secure the appointment of Lana Zaki Nusseibeh, its senior diplomat and former ambassador to the United Nations, as the next UN secretary-general. The UAE formally nominated Nusseibeh on October 21, 2026, to succeed António Guterres, whose term ends on December 31. She previously served as the UAE's permanent representative to the UN from 2013 to 2024 and has been among the country's most prominent diplomatic voices defending Abu Dhabi's foreign policy positions. Nusseibeh has repeatedly rejected allegations that the UAE provides military, logistical or financial support to the RSF, maintaining that her country's engagement in Sudan is humanitarian and directed towards ending the conflict. Her record has already attracted criticism from human rights organizations, which argue that her public statements have dismissed or undermined findings by UN investigators documenting alleged Emirati involvement in Sudan. On October 28, HRW published a statement titled UAE: UN Secretary-General Candidate Whitewashed Abuses ⁠, accusing Nusseibeh of repeatedly denying and diverting attention from evidence of her government's alleged support for the RSF and abuses linked to UAE involvement in Yemen. HRW cited her previous statements rejecting allegations of Emirati military support to the RSF, including her 2024 response to CNN that the accusations were "categorically untrue." The organization also questioned whether her record of defending UAE government positions would undermine her ability to independently lead the UN and uphold the integrity of its investigative mechanisms. During an October 27 interactive dialogue with UN member states and civil society representatives, Nusseibeh was challenged over her previous denials of UN findings concerning the UAE's alleged links to the RSF. She did not directly address the question of whether she would continue rejecting those findings if appointed secretary-general. Instead, she said she had taken leave from her UAE government responsibilities while pursuing the candidacy and would refer questions concerning the UAE to its government. Speaking to The New York Times , Cameron Hudson, a former C.I.A. analyst and director for African affairs at the National Security Council, said the continued Emirati denials of support to the RSF "make a mockery" of the investigative mechanisms that Ms. Nusseibeh now seeks to lead. "She played a significant role in obfuscating her government's contribution to atrocities in Sudan," he said. "That ought to disqualify her from any further consideration." Sudan has consistently accused Abu Dhabi of financing, arming and providing political and logistical backing to the paramilitary group. The UAE rejects the accusations. ethiopia.summary: A confidential UN report reveals that a UAE-based security firm, Global Security Services Group (GSSG), allegedly hired hundreds of Colombian mercenaries to support Sudan's Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in their conflict against the Sudanese Armed Forces. This recruitment operation, which reportedly involved the Colombian fighters being organized into a battalion called the "Desert Wolves," raises significant concerns about the UAE's involvement in the ongoing violence in Sudan, where tens of thousands have died and millions have been displaced since the conflict began in April 2023. The findings complicate the UAE's nomination of diplomat Lana Nusseibeh for the UN Secretary-General position, as she has previously denied allegations of Emirati military support to the RSF. Human rights organizations have called for investigations into GSSG and the recruitment network, emphasizing the need for accountability regarding external military support contributing to the humanitarian crisis in Sudan. The UAE has denied all allegations of involvement in the conflict. (157 words)

ethiopia.title: AI, Terrorism Top AU-EU Security Talks in Addis Ababa
ethiopia.content: Africa: AI, Terrorism Top AU-EU Security Talks in Addis Ababa - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Africa: AI, Terrorism Top AU-EU Security Talks in Addis Ababa 6 November 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) By Bruhan Makong Nairobi — The African Union (AU) and European Union (EU) are seeking to strengthen coordinated responses to Africa's evolving security challenges, with maritime insecurity, terrorism and the growing influence of artificial intelligence emerging as key priorities for cooperation. The two regional blocs opened their 9th Annual Joint Retreat between the AU Peace and Security Council (AUPSC) and the EU Political and Security Committee (EUPSC) on Thursday at the AU Commission Headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The meeting brings together members of both councils to deliberate on shared security concerns and explore ways of strengthening institutional cooperation in addressing persistent and emerging threats across the continent. Discussions are centred on four priority areas: maritime security, countering terrorism and violent extremism in Africa, artificial intelligence governance in relation to peace and security, and the Women, Peace and Security agenda. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The inclusion of artificial intelligence governance reflects growing attention to the implications of emerging technologies for security, conflict prevention and peacebuilding, while maritime security and counterterrorism remain central to efforts to address instability across Africa. The retreat is co-chaired by Côte d'Ivoire's Permanent Representative to the AU, Ambassador Antonin B. Bieke, who is also the AU Peace and Security Council Chairperson for November 2026, and the EU Political and Security Committee's Permanent Chair, Ambassador Lene Mandel Vensild. Opening remarks were delivered by AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security Bankole Adeoye and Ireland's Representative to the EU Political and Security Committee, Ambassador Luke Feeney. In a statement, the AU Department of Political Affairs, Peace and Security said the engagement provides a platform for strategic dialogue and enhanced institutional cooperation between the two organisations. "The ongoing engagement underscores the longstanding AU-EU strategic partnership and the shared commitment to strengthening coordinated responses to emerging and persistent peace and security challenges across Africa,"AUPSC said. The discussions come amid continuing security challenges across Africa, including terrorism and violent extremism, which have affected parts of the Sahel, the Horn of Africa and other regions. The AU and EU have maintained a longstanding strategic partnership on peace and security, with the joint retreat providing an avenue for aligning priorities and strengthening cooperation between their respective security institutions. somalia.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court has declared the recent extension of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term as unlawful, intensifying the ongoing power struggle in the country. The court's ruling comes amid rising tensions and political instability, as various factions contest the legitimacy of the government's actions. The term extension, which was initially proposed to address security concerns and facilitate elections, has faced widespread criticism from opposition groups and civil society. The ruling is expected to exacerbate divisions within the political landscape, as it undermines the president's authority and raises questions about the future of governance in Somalia. Observers fear that this decision could lead to further unrest and complicate efforts to stabilize the nation, which has been grappling with challenges such as terrorism, humanitarian crises, and political fragmentation. The situation remains fluid, with potential implications for both domestic and international stakeholders involved in Somalia's political affairs.

Farah Abdi Warsameh - AP Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save MOGADISHU, Somalia (AP) — Somalia’s power struggle has deepened after the Supreme Court ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s term had expired and ordered elections within 90 days. The court's decision on Thursday came a day after Mohamud dismissed the country's chief justice. The presidency had not responded to the ruling by Friday. The confrontation comes a week after the United Nations closed its political mission , which had helped rival leaders negotiate. No replacement mediator has been agreed upon for an election dispute that has already sparked armed clashes in the capital, Mogadishu. Court rejects another year in power The Supreme Court's five-page judgment, reviewed by The Associated Press, rejected the president’s position that constitutional changes allow him to remain in office until 2027. The court said parliament’s decision to extend presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years did not give current officeholders another year in power. It ruled that their terms had already expired. Judges gave political leaders 30 days to agree on how to hold elections and limited the government to routine administration pending a vote. They did not name a replacement president or specify what would happen if the deadlines were missed. In announcing Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed’s dismissal, the presidency cited complaints about the administration of justice and the need for judicial reform. The Supreme Court rejected his removal, saying the president had violated the constitution and accusing him of trying to obstruct its review of the term extensions. Local news outlet Hiiraan Online reported Friday that government troops had deployed around the Supreme Court on Thursday and that the chief justice had been ordered to leave. The AP could not independently verify the report. Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, who brought the challenge, welcomed the judgment and urged the president to negotiate. Adnan Abdi Ali, a political analyst at the Somali Center for Studies in Mogadishu, questioned whether the ruling would be enforced. “This ruling is unlikely to be implemented, as it comes at a time of ongoing electoral disputes,” he said. The dispute also concerns how Somalis will vote. The president wants direct elections to replace a system in which clan representatives choose lawmakers, who then elect the president. Opposition leaders and the regional governments of Puntland and Jubaland have challenged his constitutional and electoral changes. Troop withdrawal adds security uncertainty Ugandan troops had been deployed under a bilateral agreement with Somalia that helped recapture and hold territory against al-Qaida-linked al-Shabab militants. African Union peacekeepers plan to replace them at four bases critical to protecting Mogadishu, but it remains unclear who will secure the positions those peacekeepers leave behind. Uganda says its remaining forces, including AU peacekeepers, will leave by the end of 2027. Al-Shabab still controls large rural areas and attacks Mogadishu and other cities. Ahead of the U.N. political mission’s closure, Mohamed Husein Gaas, director of the Mogadishu-based RAAD Peace Research Institute, warned that competing claims to power could undermine cooperation among security forces. “Somalia could find itself confronting a political crisis without an agreed mechanism to contain it,” he told the AP. Associated Press writer Khaled Kazziha in Nairobi, Kenya, contributed to this report. somalia.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court has declared President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension unlawful, intensifying the ongoing power struggle in the country. The court ruled that Mohamud's term had expired and mandated elections within 90 days, following his dismissal of the chief justice just a day prior. The ruling contradicts the president's claim that constitutional amendments allowed him to remain in office until 2027. The court's decision comes amid escalating tensions, particularly after the closure of the UN's political mission, which had facilitated negotiations among rival factions. The judges have given political leaders 30 days to agree on an election process while limiting the government's actions to routine administration. The situation remains precarious, with concerns about the enforcement of the ruling and the potential for further conflict, especially as armed clashes have already erupted in the capital, Mogadishu. The political landscape is further complicated by differing views on electoral processes and security challenges posed by the militant group al-Shabab.

somalia.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court has ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension is unlawful, declaring that his term has expired and mandating elections within 90 days. This decision intensifies the ongoing power struggle in the country, which has faced political instability and challenges in governance. The ruling comes amid a backdrop of heightened tensions and concerns over the electoral process, as the nation grapples with security issues, including threats from the militant group Al-Shabaab. The court's order for immediate elections aims to restore democratic processes, but it also raises questions about the potential for further conflict among political factions. As the situation unfolds, the international community is closely monitoring developments in Somalia, hoping for a peaceful resolution that can lead to stability and effective governance in the region.

somalia.summary: Somalia is making its debut at the China International Import Expo (CIIE) with over 40 companies participating in the event held in Shanghai. Gamal Mohamed Hassan, Somalia's Minister of Commerce and Industry, emphasized the primary objective of the participation is to forge connections between Somali businesses and Chinese partners, leveraging China's zero-tariff policy. He highlighted key Somali exports such as seafood, frankincense, and minerals, showcasing the country's readiness to engage in trade with China. In addition to the expo, Somali businesses plan to visit other Chinese provinces and participate in a business forum to strengthen partnerships. This initiative marks a significant step for Somalia in enhancing its international trade relations and promoting its products on a global platform.

Commerce and Industry Minister Jamal Mohamed Hassan opened the pavilion, where Somali companies are showcasing sesame, frankincense and myrrh, the commerce ministry said. China has granted zero-tariff access on all goods to Somalia as one of 33 least developed African countries since December 2024, and in May extended the treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic ties, according to China’s Customs Tariff Commission. “This means goods exported from Somalia will always be cheaper than goods exported from Asian countries or elsewhere,” Somalia’s ambassador to China, Hodan Osman Abdi, said. Hassan said Chinese buyers had shown strong interest in Somali agricultural products, livestock, fish and sesame. Abdi said Somalia was focusing on industrialisation and wanted to export processed rather than raw materials, with several companies showing processed and packaged consumer products. Securing a place at the expo was the biggest challenge, she said, as Somalia had not taken part in any of its previous eight editions. Work began last year and approval came only around April. During the expo, which runs until Nov. 10, Somali traders will meet buyers and companies from China and other countries to find new markets, the ministry said. I'm here to help you understand this article. Ask me anything about the content! Send By Ben Farmer, Uganda has begun withdrawing thousands of troops from Somalia, heightening questions about whether the local government can overcome one of al-Qaeda’s most successful affiliates. Kampala announced its first troops had already been pulled back after it had spent nearly 20 years helping battle Islamist insurgents in the Horn of Africa nation. All Ugandan troops are due out of the country by the end of 2027, leaving a significant gap in an international mission to bolster Somalia against al-Shabaab fighters. The future of international operations to stabilise the country has already been put in doubt by plans from key backers such as the United States to withdraw funding. Uganda had deployed 4,500-6,000 troops in Somalia as part of the latest African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) mission and a further 2,000-2,500 under a separate bilateral agreement. The latter troops are the ones departing first. Ugandan peacekeepers at an AUSSOM recognition ceremony in Mogadishu, November 2025. One senior former international official in Somalia told NSN: “Not only is Uganda going, but they were among the few nations who did any fighting. “There’s always been a fear that any pull out would end up in Al-Shabaab taking more ground. Potentially, it’s going to be a mess.” Somalia’s allies have become increasingly disillusioned by the federal government’s lack of progress fighting al-Shabaab and by endless political infighting. Divisions between the central government and the regional administrations have hampered efforts to improve the security situation and elections in 2027 are expected to be contentious. A statement from Uganda’s military said: “The Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) will gradually withdraw all its forces in Somalia, including those currently deployed under AUSSOM by the close of 2027. “This will mark the end of Uganda’s enduring 20-year peace and stabilisation support operations in Somalia, permitting the Somali Armed Forces to assume full responsibility for security in the country.” Somalia’s president, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, is reported to have last month met his Ugandan counterpart, Yoweri Museveni, in an unsuccessful attempt to delay the withdrawal. Somalia’s central government said its own troops were moving into bases in the port town of Barawe and Shalambood as Ugandan troops left. Analysis from the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said the Ugandans had made steady progress in securing territory initially seized by al-Shabaab in South West state from mid-2025, but insecurity had flared in recent months. The drawdown coincides with uncertainty about funding for AUSSOM. Washington earlier this year said it would cut logistical funding to the UN support mission in Somalia which is a central pillar of support to the peacekeepers. America later gave a temporary reprieve. EIC said: “Nonetheless, funding gaps, as well as the inefficient substitution of troops, threaten to reverse gains made against al-Shabaab.” African Union and Somali troops during the handover of Xaaji Cali military base in June 2023. (Source – United Nations Support Office in Somalia) Al-Shabaab, meaning The Youth in Arabic, emerged as the radical wing of Somalia’s now-defunct Union of Islamic Courts, which controlled Mogadishu in 2006, before being forced out by Ethiopian forces. The group vows to implement Islamic law and condemns democracy as a Western transplant. In 2012 the leadership swore allegiance to al-Qaeda. Follow on Google News Follow on X (Twitter) Share. somalia.summary: Uganda has commenced the withdrawal of its troops from Somalia, raising concerns about the ability of the Somali government to combat al-Shabaab, an affiliate of al-Qaeda. After nearly 20 years of military support, Uganda plans to fully withdraw its forces by the end of 2027. This includes approximately 4,500-6,000 troops deployed under the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) and an additional 2,000-2,500 under a bilateral agreement, with the latter group being the first to leave. The withdrawal coincides with growing disillusionment among Somalia's allies regarding the federal government's effectiveness in addressing security issues and ongoing political strife. As Ugandan troops depart, Somali forces are moving into their bases, but analysts warn that the exit could lead to increased al-Shabaab activity. The situation is further complicated by potential funding cuts from key supporters like the United States, which could undermine ongoing stabilization efforts in the region.

الأربعاء 4 نوفمبر، على ملعب "كيغالي بيليه" ضمن الجولة السابعة من الدوري الرواندي، الذي يشهد مشاركة الهلال ومواطنه المريخ . وفرط "الموج الأزرق" في فرصة تحقيق الفوز، مكتفيا بالتعادل بعد أن بادر بالتسجيل عبر قائده وهدافه محمد عبد الرحمن، قبل أن يدرك المنافس التعادل في الرمق الأخير من المباراة، ليهدر الفريق فرصة مثالية لتقليص الفارق مع صدارة الدوري، في انتظار خوض مبارياته المؤجلة الثلاث. مكاسب مضاعفة لـ"غربال" رغم تفريط الهلال في الفوز باستقباله هدف التعادل في اللحظات الأخيرة، إلا أن "الكابيتانو" محمد عبد الرحمن نجح في وضع فريقه بالمقدمة بهدف رائع، محققا مكاسب شخصية بتعزيز سجله التهديفي وتأكيد عودته القوية قبل المواجهات المرتقبة في مجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا عقب فترة التوقف الدولي. كما سيمنح مدرب المنتخب "كواسي أبياه" خياراً هجومياً مميزاً لاستعادة فاعلية "صقور الجديان" التهديفية، بخوضه مباراتين حاسمتين أمام المنتخب السنغالي بتصفيات بطولة الأمم الأفريقية. اقرأ أيضًا مدرب الهلال السوداني يكشف أزمة قاتلة قبل دوري أبطال أفريقيا رامي كمال: الهلال يستحق تكريمًا سياديًا وسنتوج باللقب القاري وسيحظى مدرب النادي الأزرق بفرصة مثالية لتجهيز عناصره عبر خوض تجارب ودية قوية خلال فترة التوقف الدولي، إذ سيلتحق 16 من أبرز نجومه بمنتخباتهم الوطنية، منهم 13 لاعبا في صفوف "صقور الجديان", و3 آخرون مع منتخبات بلدانهم. وسيعمل المدرب خلال هذا الغياب على إعداد البدائل، سعيا لتحقيق أفضل النتائج في دور المجموعات بدوري أبطال أفريقيا. وقرر المدرب جوزيف زينباور استغلال فترة التوقف بإجراء مباريات إعدادية، على أن يخوض الفريق مواجهة واحدة في الدوري الرواندي عقب التوقف، ليبدأ بعدها رحلة شاقة في دوري أبطال أفريقيا بملاقاة حوريا كوناكري الغيني في 28 نوفمبر الجاري، ثم يحل ضيفا على المغرب الفاسي في 5 أبطال أفريقيا الهلال السوداني مصطفى كرشوم الدوري السوداني الممتاز كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin أضفنا الى 'غوغل' وصف الألماني جوزيف زينباور مدرب الهلال السوداني، نتيجة التعادل (1-1) التي حققها فريقه أمام رايون سبورت الرواندي في الجولة السابعة من مسابقة الدوري الرواندي بالسيئة، مؤكدا أن فريقه فرط في فوز كان في المتناول بعد تقدمه المبكر، قبل التعهد بمعالجة السلبيات التي رافقت أداء الفريق في المباريات الأخيرة. وأوضح المدرب عبر مقطع فيديو نشره الموقع الرسمي للنادي، أنه لم يحظ بفرصة كافية لخوض تجارب ودية قبل انطلاقة الموسم للوقوف على إمكانات جميع اللاعبين، خاصة مع انضمام عناصر جديدة خلال فترة الانتقالات الصيفية، مشيرًا إلى أن فترة التوقف الدولي ستساعده في تجهيز الفريق بشكل أفضل. مدرب الهلال يشيد بنجميه كما أشاد زينباور بنجميه سفيان فريد و مصطفى كرشوم ، قائلا: "قدم الحارس سفيان مباراة متميزة، ويعد كرشوم مدافعا رائعا يمتاز بالهدوء والقدرة الفائقة على استخلاص الكرة وبناء اللعب". وأضاف: "تقدمنا مبكرا ولم نستثمر الفرص التي أتيحت لنا، واستقبلنا هدفا في الرمق الأخير من المباراة؛ كان يتعين علينا تسجيل هدفين على الأقل لنحسم المباراة، ولكننا لم نستثمر الفرص، علينا إيجاد حلول لاستقبال الأهداف المتأخرة، وبالمجمل، لست راضيا عن هذه النتيجة". اقرأ أيضًا رامي كمال: الهلال يستحق تكريمًا سياديًا وسنتوج باللقب القاري المريخ يربك تحضيرات الهلال لمجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا كما كشف زينباور عن أسباب تذبذب الأداء والتغييرات المستمرة في تشكيل فريقه مؤخرًا، قائلا: "لقد أضفنا عناصر جديدة خلال فترة الانتقالات، لدينا لاعبون شباب نرغب في منحهم فرصة المشاركة؛ لذا نجري هذه التعديلات لنقف على مستوياتهم، ونأمل أن يقدموا الإضافة المرجوة". وأضاف: "واجهنا منافسين أقوياء، على غرار فريق رايون الذي تميز باللياقة العالية والقوة البدنية، وسنواجه تحديات صعبة تستدعي وفرة في العناصر". وختم المدرب الألماني حديثه قائلاً: "نسعى لمزيد من التطور، ويتعين علينا مواصلة العمل الجاد لاستثمار الفرص في تطوير الجوانب البدنية والتكتيكية قبل المباريات الصعبة التي تنتظرنا في دوري أبطال أفريقيا ، إذ يجب أن نستعد جيدا لنبلغ مرحلة متميزة من الجاهزية حتى نتمكن من مجابهة التحديات المرتقبة". النشرة البريدية اشترك football.title: الهلال السوداني يواجه رايون سبورت بالقوة الضاربة.. وزينباور يرفض المغامرة بالبدلاء - تاق برس
football.content: الهلال السوداني يواجه رايون سبورت بالقوة الضاربة.. وزينباور يرفض المغامرة بالبدلاء — تاق برس اعجاب المتابعين الجمعة, نوفمبر 6, 2026 من نحن السياسة التحريرية للإعلان على تاق برس اتصل بنا تاق برس - اخبار السودان والعالم الرئيسية أخبار عاجلة سياسية منوعات وثقافة إقتصاد رياضة علوم وتكنلوجيا مقالات أخري تقارير صحة الرئيسية أخبار رياضة الهلال السوداني يواجه رايون سبورت بالقوة الضاربة.. وزينباور يرفض المغامرة بالبدلاء الهلال السوداني يواجه رايون سبورت بالقوة الضاربة.. وزينباور يرفض المغامرة بالبدلاء بواسطة editor في نوفمبر 3, 2026 288 مشاركة متابعات تاق برس – يستعد الهلال السوداني لخوض مواجهة مهمة أمام رايون سبورت الرواندي، غداً الأربعاء، ضمن منافسات الجولة الثامنة من الدوري الرواندي الممتاز، في مباراة يتطلع خلالها الفريق إلى مواصلة انتصاراته وتعزيز موقعه في جدول الترتيب. ويتجه المدير الفني للهلال، الألماني جوزيف زينباور، بحسب صحيفة آكشن سبورت، إلى الاعتماد على عناصره الأساسية، رافضاً تكرار تجربة الدفع بتشكيلة يغلب عليها البدلاء، التي كلفت الفريق خسارة ثقيلة أمام مارين بثلاثة أهداف دون مقابل. ويستعيد زينباور موقعه في المنطقة الفنية بعد انتهاء عقوبة إيقافه لمباراة واحدة، وسط اتجاه للاعتماد على عدد من العناصر الأساسية، من بينهم مصطفى كرشوم وياسر عوض وأرنست لوزولو، مع التركيز على تعزيز الانضباط التكتيكي والتنظيم الدفاعي. وتكتسب المواجهة أهمية إضافية باعتبارها اختباراً مهماً للهلال قبل انطلاق مشواره في دور المجموعات لدوري أبطال أفريقيا، حيث يواجه حوريا كوناكري الغيني يوم 28 نوفمبر الجاري. وتُقام المباراة على ملعب كيغالي بيليه عند السادسة والنصف مساءً، وكان الهلال قد استأنف تدريباته بالعاصمة الرواندية كيغالي، وسط أجواء من الحماس والتركيز، استعداداً للمواجهة المرتقبة. الدوري الرواندي الممتاز الهلال السوداني كرة القدم 288 مشاركة أخبار ذات صلة رياضة الهلال السوداني في مجموعة نارية.. تعرف على منافسيه في دوري أبطال إفريقيا رياضة الهلال السوداني يقترب من مجموعات الأبطال بفوز ثمين خارج أرضه أمام سيداما الإثيوبي رياضة برشلونة يحطم رقماً تاريخياً في الدوري الإسباني بعد 76 عاماً رياضة غياب مفاجئ لفيرجيل فان ديك عن تشكيلة ليفربول الاساسية رياضة مالين: متحمّس لمواجهة ريال مدريد رياضة مسؤولون في البريمييرليغ يدرسون تعليق مشاركة مانشستر سيتي رياضة الدوري الاسباني: ريال بيتيس يحقق فوزا عريضا ومستحقا على أوساسونا رياضة غوارديولا يعود لملعب الاتحاد لمشاهدة مانشستر سيتي رياضة مودريتش يعترف بشعوره بالعار بعد «ليلة كارثية» لكرواتيا رياضة ريان بابل: الونسو سيتولى قيادة ليفربول مستقبلاً جاري التحميل ... تحميل المزيد لا مزيد من المشاركات تابعنا على
